goal: Stop the node from disconnecting good peers during IBD just because they were too busy serving requested blocks to answer a ping in time.
Fixes real unnecessary disconnections seen when downloading over multiple slow-bandwidth peers.

categories.name: p2p
why: P2 because it fixes real-world wrongful disconnections of well-behaved peers during IBD, a reliability issue affecting anyone syncing with limited bandwidth across many peers.
Other timeout mechanisms already backstop misbehaving peers, so the fix narrows scope to a genuine false-positive rather than removing protection.

result.summary: This PR suspends the p2p ping timeout while a peer is actively serving requested blocks, adding a short grace period after the last new block before the timeout resumes. It moves the ping-timeout disconnect check out of MaybeSendPing into SendMessages so it can access per-peer block-in-flight state, and adds a new functional test (p2p_ping_ibd.py) exercising the scenario.
result.problem: During IBD with bandwidth split across many peers, a well-behaved peer can be busy serving requested blocks (which are prioritized over other messages) and fail to answer a ping within 20 minutes, causing the node to wrongly disconnect it even though the peer did nothing wrong. This is described in linked issue #35761.

resolved_concerns: l0rinc's nit about test ordering to show before/after behavior was addressed by moving parts of the test into the first commit.

danielabrozzoni's concern about m_last_block_time not updating for already-known blocks, potentially shortening grace period, was judged a fringe one-off scenario by the author and not pushed back on.
danielabrozzoni's concern about a user-triggered ping RPC resetting ping_start and masking a due disconnect was accepted as an existing, unlikely edge case not worth fixing.
danielabrozzoni's test robustness suggestion (checking no disconnect within grace period while blocks are still in flight) was implemented by the author on 2026-09-16.

result.card: This PR suspends the p2p ping-timeout disconnect check while a peer is actively serving requested blocks during IBD, adding a short grace period afterward before the timeout resumes. It fixes a real bug (linked issue #35761) where honest peers get wrongly disconnected because block-serving is prioritized over answering pings when bandwidth is split across many peers during IBD. Strongest evidence of importance: the PR description and linked issue show this happens to well-behaved peers 'although they have done nothing wrong,' and other timeout mechanisms (block download timeout, stalling, socket inactivity) remain in place as backstops. No dependencies block this PR; it directly resolves #35761.
